questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Distinguish between correlation and causation
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Cities with more ice-cream sales also have more sunburns. Does buying ice cream cause sunburns? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
Cities with more ice-cream sales also have more sunburns.
Does buying ice cream cause sunburns? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. Both go up in hot, sunny weather; a third variable explains the association.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Distinguish between correlation and causation
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A study finds that students who sleep more tend to have higher grades. Can you conclude that more sleep causes higher grades? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A study finds that students who sleep more tend to have higher grades.
Can you conclude that more sleep causes higher grades? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. The data show an association, not a cause; a randomized experiment is needed to show cause.
